### Handling Adversity
Author: Charles R. Swindoll
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/todays-insight-chuck-swindoll/today-s-insight-august-28-2019.html
Passage: Job 1:21-22
Points:
- In a matter of hours, Job suffered sudden and devastating losses of all his children, wealth, and servants.
- Rather than responding with bitterness or blaming God, Job acknowledged the Lord's sovereign right over what He gives and takes away.
- He persevered through tragedy by looking beyond earthly pain toward the hope of the resurrection.
- Job humbly admitted his own lack of understanding rather than demanding answers to why he was suffering.
- Entrusting unexplainable adversity to God keeps believers grounded and prevents destructive responses.

### The Lord Gave and Took Away: Lessons on Suffering from Job
Author: Vaneetha Rendall Risner
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/the-lord-gave-and-took-away
Passage: Job 1:21
Points:
- Job's response to crushing loss proves that God Himself is our reward, not the gifts He gives us.
- Worshiping God in the middle of severe affliction displays His supreme value before the unseen heavenly realms.
- Suffering cannot touch believers apart from God's sovereign permission, assuring us that our trials have divine purpose.
- The loss of earthly blessings often clears away distractions so we can know God far more profoundly.
- Choosing to praise the Lord during sorrow deepens our love and securely binds us to Him.
